BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r4.claim: God tested Mecca’s people with seven years of famine after the Prophet’s supplication; they ate carrion, hides, bones, and blood in ingratitude.
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى أنا ابتلينا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع سبع سنين

BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r5.claim: The owners were people of Ṣanʿāʾ, identified by one source as three brothers; reported locations include Darwān near Ṣanʿāʾ and Yemen.
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r5.anchor: وأصحاب الجنة قوم من أهل صنعاء وفي كشف الأسرار سه برادر بودند

BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r6.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r6.claim: Al-Suhaylī locates the orchard at Darwān, several farsakhs from Ṣanʿāʾ.
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r6.anchor: وقال السهيلي : هي جنة بضروان وضروان

BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r7.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r7.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān locates it in Yemen shortly after Jesus was raised; the generous father kept a year’s provisions and gave the surplus to the poor at harvest.
BURSEVI:v10p86#2/r7.anchor: وفي فتح الرحمن الجنة بستان يقال له ضروان باليمن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r3.claim: The orchard parable warns Quraysh that present peace and blessings do not last: God can remove them suddenly and leave people to face the consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r3.anchor: the peace and security they have today should not mislead them to think that they would remain under the same conditions forever

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r2.claim: The orchard parable exposes the hollowness of Quraysh leaders’ authority: God can remove it instantly, after which their grief and repentance will be useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r2.anchor: their authority which has made them so conceited and proud that they are making fun of the warnings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r3.claim: The plural pronoun ‘them’ refers to the previously described people collectively, confirming that the portrait is of Quraysh leadership as a whole rather than one individual.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r3.anchor: this character is not that of a specific individual; it is that of the total leadership of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r4.claim: The definite article in ‘the orchard’ is generic in parables, painting a complete situation rather than identifying a particular orchard or historical owners in Yemen or Sana.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r4.anchor: Their purpose is only to portray the overall situation so that the reader gets to know the complete picture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r5.claim: The owners confidently swore they would harvest the next morning because they believed their orchard had survived every weather change and was secure from calamity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p431/r5.anchor: their orchard had braved various phases of weather change and had become safe and secure from all calamities

QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r11.claim: One account says a Yemeni orchard owner let the poor glean what escaped harvest; after his death, his sons refused to continue giving and God destroyed the garden.
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r11.anchor: وكان للمساكين كل ما تعداه المنجل

QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r12.claim: Another account says God replaced their garden with a better one; they then planned to harvest before dawn before the poor noticed, without saying “if God wills.”
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r12.anchor: وقيل : أبدلهم الله جنة حسنة ، فأقسموا ليصرمن جنتهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r13.claim: God tested the people addressed after the Prophet prayed against them, afflicting them with famine until they ate carrion; this is compared with the orchard owners' trial.
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r13.anchor: حين دعا عليهم النبي ، فابتلاهم الله بالجوع ، حتى أكلوا الجيف

FARRA:v3p174/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r2.claim: The garden owners were people of Yemen; their father left gleanings, fallen dates, and unpicked grapes for the poor, widows, and orphans.
FARRA:v3p174/r2.anchor: كان لرجل منهم زرع، ونخل، وكرم

FARRA:v3p174/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r3.claim: After their father's death, the sons decided to stop giving because their dependents had grown and wealth shrunk; they planned to harvest in the late-night darkness so the poor would receive nothing.
FARRA:v3p174/r3.anchor: فإنا ندع ذلك، ثم تآمروا أن يصرموا في سدف: في ظلمة- باقية من الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed that God tighten His grip on Muḍar and impose years of famine like Joseph's years; Abū Ḥayyān cites this before the garden parable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r1.anchor: اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر واجعلها عليهم سنين كسني يوسف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.claim: One account places the garden in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ; its owner paid God's due, but his sons withheld it after inheriting and the garden was destroyed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.anchor: كانت بأرض اليمن بالقرب منهم قريبا من صنعاء لرجل كان يؤدي حق الله منها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.claim: Another account locates it at Ṣurawān near Ṣanʿāʾ after Jesus; the owner left poor neighbors dates and grapes missed by harvesters, but his sons decided to stop sharing because they had dependents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.anchor: وكان صاحبها ينزل للمساكنين ما أخطأه المنجل وما في أسفل الأكراس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.claim: The sons swore to harvest early in darkness and secretly, keeping the poor from their customary share; the oath's response predicts that they would cut the crop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.anchor: فحلفوا ليصرمنها مصبحين في السدف خفية من المساكين،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.claim: They swore they would gather the garden's fruit in the morning and did not make an exception.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.anchor: {إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين * ولا يستثنون} أي حلفوا ليجذن ثمرها صباحا؛ ولم يستثنوا.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r1.claim: God tested the people of Mecca with drought following the Prophet's prayer against Mudar for years like Joseph's years.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r1.anchor: أصبنا أهل مكة ببلية وهي القحط بدعوة رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وقوله اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r2.claim: In كما بلونا, kāf marks an implied cognate accusative and ما is a verbal noun; alternatively ما means الذي.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r2.anchor: فالكاف في محل نصب مصدر مقدر وما مصدرية وقيل بمعنى الذي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r3.claim: The Garden was a familiar orchard near the people in Yemen; its owner used to give God's due, but his heirs withheld its produce from the poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r3.anchor: كانت بأرض اليمن بالقرب منهم قريبا من صنعاء لرجل كان يؤدي حق الله تعالى منها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir's report places the garden in Sawran, Yemen, six miles from Sanʿa.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن جرير بأرض في اليمن يقال لها صوران بينها وبين صنعاء ستة أميال

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the owners were Abyssinians whose father fed the poor; after he died, his sons called him foolish and vowed to feed no poor person.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس هم ناس من الحبشة كانت لأبيهم جنة وكان يطعم منها المساكين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r6.claim: Qatada says an Israelite elder gave away his annual surplus, despite his sons' objections, and his sons vowed to stop the charity after his death.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال كانت لشيخ من بني إسرائيل وكان يمسك قوت سنته ويتصدق بالفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r7.claim: Another account says the owner left gleanings and leftover fruit for the poor; after his death, his sons feared for their dependents and secretly vowed to harvest early.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r7.anchor: وكان يترك للمساكين ما أخطأه المنجل وما في أسفل الأكداس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r8.claim: The phrase إذ أقسموا is grammatically governed by بلونا.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p29#2/r8.anchor: كما قال عز وجل ﴿ إذ أقسموا ﴾ معمول لبلونا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30/r1.claim: They swore to cut the fruit once ripe, entering the morning; the wording reports their oath rather than quoting it directly, since a direct quotation would use first-person plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30/r1.anchor: ﴿ مصبحين ﴾ داخلين في الصباح وهذا حكاية لقسمهم لا على منطوقهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r1.claim: God tested Mecca’s people with drought and hunger, as He tested the owners of the garden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r1.anchor: {إنا بلوناهم} يعني اختبرنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع {كما بلونا} ابتلينا {أصحاب الجنة}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that a pious owner’s garden near Sanaa allowed poor people gleanings after harvest; his three heirs, deeming wealth too small for many dependents, swore to harvest before the poor without saying ‘if God wills,’ then found the garden burned black overnight.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: في قوله عز وجل: "إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة" قال: كان بستان باليمن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r3.claim: ليصرمنها means they planned to cut and gather the fruit in the morning, before the poor learned of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r3.anchor: أليجذنها وليقطعن ثمرها إذا أصبحوا قبل أن يعلم المساكين

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r2.claim: God tested Meccans with drought as He tested garden owners outside Sanʿāʾ; their righteous father let the poor glean after harvest, but his heirs feared poverty and planned a secret dawn harvest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r2.anchor: { إنا بلونهم } بلونا أهل مكة شرفها الله تعالى، بالقحط. { كما بلونا أصحب الجنة } يريد البستان

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r3.claim: The father left poor people what the sickle missed and wind dropped, or the substantial crop gathered under a palm; the sons swore to cut it early while hiding from the poor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:16-17/r3.anchor: وكان ينادي الفقراء وقت الصرام ويترك لهم ما أخطأه المنجل وألقته الريح

BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.claim: The surah is early Meccan except verses 17–33 and 48–50, and is commonly placed after al-ʿAlaq as the second revelation; despite ordering disputes it reflects the first revelation’s atmosphere.
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.anchor: السورة مكية مبكرة، إلا آيات (17: 33، 48: 50) فمدنية

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.claim: The apparent story is that the garden owners planned to harvest everything at dawn and leave nothing; the author rejects the gloss that they merely omitted saying in shāʾ Allāh.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.anchor: وظاهر النص، أن خطيئتهم التي أخذوا بها، هي التصميم على صرم جنتهم خفية

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.anchor: أن هذه الجنة كانت لرجل صالح، حدودا قومه وبلده فقيل إنه من أهل اليمن

BINTSHATI:v2p65/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r3.claim: The plural pronoun in we tested them refers to the deniers and every oath-breaking, contemptible person.
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r3.anchor: عائد على المكذبين وكل حلاف مهين

BINTSHATI:v2p65/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r4.claim: One interpretation compares Quraysh's trial to the garden owners' punishment by citing the seven-year famine, when Quraysh ate hides.
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r4.anchor: قول من قالوا: النازل بقريش المماثل لأمر الجنة، هو الجدب

BINTSHATI:v2p65/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r5.claim: Another interpretation compares the garden owners' planned deprivation of the poor with Quraysh's vow before Badr to kill the Prophet and his companions, followed by their defeat.
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r5.anchor: تشبيه بلاء قريش ببلاء أصحاب الجنة، هو أن أهل الجنة عزموا

BINTSHATI:v2p65/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r6.claim: The Badr interpretation reads later history into the passage, since Badr occurred about five years after this surah; the warning addresses tyrants generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p65/r6.anchor: النص، على أي حال، صريح في ردع كل الطغاة المتجبرين

NAHHAS:v5p9/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p9/r12.claim: God tested the garden owners by requiring gratitude and payment of the poor's obligatory due.
NAHHAS:v5p9/r12.anchor: أي تعبدناهم بالشكر على النعم وإعطاء الفقراء حقوقهم التي أوجبناها في أموالهم

NAHHAS:v5p9/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p9/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the garden owners were People of the Book.
NAHHAS:v5p9/r13.anchor: ( كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة ) قال ابن عباس هم أهل الكتاب

NAHHAS:v5p9/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p9/r14.claim: Yaṣrimannahā means they would cut and gather it; jadādh means cutting, while muṣbiḥīn is circumstantial and means entering the morning.
NAHHAS:v5p9/r14.anchor: أي ليجذنها والجذاذ القطع ومنه صرم فلان فينا وسيف صارم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r1.claim: God tests Quraysh and others by granting worldly ease; they mistake this for divine favor and look down on poor believers, though meeting the Prophet itself tests whether they act well or badly.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r2.claim: The testing may also refer to the famine the Prophet invoked against Mecca; even after eating carrion, its people did not repent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r2.anchor: أو كان ابتلاؤنا لهم بالقحط الذي دعا عليهم به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أكلوا الجيف فما تابوا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r3.claim: The famous orchard lay near Sanaa at al-Darwan; its owner customarily left fallen or missed fruit for the poor, but his sons resolved to harvest before sunrise so no poor person could claim any.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r3.anchor: كان صاحبه ينادي الفقراء وقت الصرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r4.claim: The expression for cutting the orchard conveys a decisive, complete severing that would prevent the poor from sharing its fruit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r4.anchor: عبر به عن الجذاذ بدلالته على القطع البائن المعزوم عليه المستأثل

DURR-FULL:v8p250/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r5.claim: Qatada says these are people whose story God has recounted and made clear.
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة}

DURR-FULL:v8p250/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Abu Jahl ordered the captives at Badr bound in the mountains rather than killed; the verse likens his power over them to the garden owners' power over their orchard.

DURR-FULL:v8p250/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the owners of the garden as People of the Book.

DURR-FULL:v8p250/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r10.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr locates the garden in a place in Yemen called Dar, six miles from Sana'a.
DURR-FULL:v8p250/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Abu Jahl ordered captives at Badr to be bound in the mountains rather than killed; the verse compares their power over opponents to the owners' power over their garden.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج ان أبا جهل قال : يوم بدر : خذوهم اخذا واربطوهم في الجبال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the garden's owners were Abyssinians whose father fed the poor, but after his death his sons called him foolish and planned to harvest without giving alms.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3365#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : كما بلونا اصحاب الجنة قال : هم ناس من الحبشة كانت لابيهم جنة وكان يطعم منها السائلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r1.claim: A reported interpretation sees the threatened mark on the nose as a humiliation on Judgment Day, because the man displayed arrogance and pride through his nose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r1.anchor: وقيل هذا وعيد بتشويه أنفه يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r2.claim: The pronoun in بلوناهم refers to the deniers previously mentioned; the orchard parable begins a new section prompted by the preceding account of wealth and children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r2.anchor: ضمير الغائيبن في قوله : { بلوناهم } يعود إلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r3.claim: The parable warns that pride in ample provision has long led people to scorn truth and neglect gratitude; similar examples appear in the Cave and the story of Qarun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r3.anchor: فضرب الله للمشركين مثلا بحال أصحاب هذه الجنة لعلهم يستفيقون من غفلتهم وغرورهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r4.claim: Their trial was through blessings: Mecca enjoyed security, abundant provision, and easy trade across distant lands, yet its people rejected the messenger and failed to reflect on their gifts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r5.claim: The Meccans resemble the orchard owners in turning from seeking God's pleasure and thanking Him for His gifts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r5.anchor: ووجه المشابهة بين حالهم وحال أصحاب الجنة المذكورة هنا هو الإعراض عن طلب مرضاة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r6.claim: The parable implicitly threatens a reversal from prosperity to distress; though the immediate cause differs, the same kind of punishment later struck the Meccans with seven famine years after the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p78/r6.anchor: وقد حصل ذلك بعد سنين إذ أخذهم الله بسبع سنين بعد هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r1.claim: The orchard story was associated with Darwan near Sanaa in Yemen; some say Darwan was the garden's name.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the large garden belonged to a righteous, believing man from the People of the Book; the source does not identify him as Jewish or Christian.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r2.anchor: غرسها رجل من أهل الصلاح والإيمان من أهل الكتاب قاله ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r3.claim: Some say its owner was Jewish, reasoning that Yemen became Jewish in Bilqis's era or later and that Torah law required a tithe from fruit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r4.claim: Others place the owners shortly after Jesus, before Christianity spread in Yemen, which they date to the Abyssinian conquest near the Year of the Elephant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : كان أصحاب هذه الجنة بعد عيسى بقليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r5.claim: Ikrima says the owners were Abyssinians: their father shared the harvest with the poor, who supported orphans and widows, but his three wealthy sons became stingy and plotted to exclude them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r5.anchor: وعن عكرمة : كانوا من الحبشة كانت لأبيهم جنة وجعل في ثمرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r6.claim: They planned to harvest before dawn before the poor arrived; their oath may have bound a hesitant brother, explaining why the middle brother later asks whether they would heed his warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r6.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن بعضهم كان مترددا في موافقتهم على ما عزموا عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r7.claim: The hesitant brother is said to have urged them to fear God, abandon their evil plan, and remember God's punishment; the others overruled him and secured the group's participation by oath.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p79/r7.anchor: قيل كان يقول لهم : اتقوا الله واعدلوا عن خبث نيتكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r8.claim: The people tested in the parable are Quraysh; the garden belonged to brothers whose father retained his own provision and gave the surplus to the poor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إنا بلوناهم يريد قريشا، أي امتحناهم، وأصحاب الجنة فيما ذكر قوم إخوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r9.claim: One account says their father took the poor with him at harvest so they could share the crop.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r9.anchor: وقيل بل كان يحمل المساكين معه في وقت حصاده وجذه، فيجذيهم منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r10.claim: After their father died, the brothers judged his generosity mistaken and resolved to harvest without admitting or giving anything to a poor person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r10.anchor: فمات الشيخ، فقال ولده: نحن جماعة وفعل أبينا كان خطأ، فلنذهب إلى جنتنا ولا يدخلها علينا مسكين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r15.claim: God likens Quraysh's test through Muhammad and his guidance to the brothers' test through their father's practice and their religious obligations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r15.anchor: فشبه الله تعالى قريشا بهم، في أنهم امتحنهم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهداه كما امتحن أولئك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.claim: As the garden owners were punished in their orchard, Quraysh face punishment in their worldly life, while repentance remains open to survivors as it was for the brothers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.anchor: فكما حل بأولئك العقاب في جنتهم كذلك يحل بهؤلاء في جميع دنياهم وفي حياتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r17.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r17.claim: Many exegetes say Quraysh's seven years of famine correspond to the brothers' loss of their garden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r17.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين: السنون السبع التي أصابت قريشا هي بمثابة ما أصاب أولئك في جنتهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r18.claim: ليصرمنها means to harvest it; صرام is picking dates or fruit from any tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r18.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ليصرمنها أي ليجدنها، وصرام النخل: جد ثمره وكذلك في كل شجرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r19.claim: مصبحين means when they entered the morning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r19.anchor: ومصبحين معناه: إذا دخلوا في الصباح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335/r1.claim: God tested the people of Mecca with hunger and drought as He tested the owners of the garden when their garden was destroyed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335/r1.anchor: يعني أهل مكة أي ابتليناهم بالجوع والقحط كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة حين هلكت جنتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r1.claim: The garden owners are an example for Quraysh: God gave them the great mercy of Muhammad’s mission and abundant blessings, but they answered with denial, rejection, and opposition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لكفار قريش فيما أهدى إليهم من الرحمة العظيمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.claim: The heirs swore to harvest at dawn so that no poor person or petitioner would learn of the crop and receive charity; they made no exception in their oath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.anchor: حلفوا فيما بينهم ليجذن ثمرها ليلا لئلا يعلم بهم فقير ولا سائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.claim: Some early scholars say the brothers lived in Yemen near Sana’a or in Abyssinia; their righteous father maintained the garden, kept a year’s provisions, and gave the surplus to the poor, but his sons called this foolish and were punished by losing crop, profit, and charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا من قرية يقال لها ضروان

JISHUMI:v10p7031/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r4.claim: Trial, testing, and examination are synonyms; God's trial is the imposition of duties so acts occur and become manifest, although He knew beforehand they would occur, so testing is figurative of His treatment of the tested person.
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r4.anchor: والابتلاء من الله هو التعبد والتكليف، فكلفهم ليظهر من أعمالهم، فيعلم الله تعالى وقوعها كما علم من قبل

JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.claim: Ṣarm is cutting, especially harvesting date fruit; ṣarām and jadhādh name the harvest, and the separation between companions is also called ṣarm.
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.anchor: والصرم: أصله: القطع، والصرام والجذاذ: قطع ثمر النخل

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.claim: The owners are blamed for denying the poor their due, swearing to do so, and omitting an exception; this supports requiring an exception when speaking about the future, since one cannot be sure the statement will come true.
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.anchor: ذمهم على منع الحق، وذمهم على القسم عليه، وذمهم على ترك الاستثناء

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.claim: Intending an evil act is itself blameworthy: they were punished for the resolve even before committing the wrong, and actually taking property and denying rights is worse.
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.anchor: أن العزم على القبيح قبيح؛ لأنهم عوقبوا على عزمهم من غير منع وظلم بالمنع

SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r1.claim: مصبحين is a circumstantial phrase for the subject of ليصرمنها and means entering the morning, as in 37:137 and the proverb about hearing of a journeyer who has arrived by morning.

SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r2.claim: The kāf in كما is an accusative adjective of an omitted verbal noun, with ما either a verbal noun or relative pronoun; إذ attaches to بلونا.
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r2.anchor: في موضع نصب نعتا لمصدر محذوف،

SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r3.claim: ليصرمنها answers the oath, but shifts person from their reported first-person words; exact quotation would be لنصرمنها.
SAMIN-DURR:68:17/r3.anchor: جواب للقسم، وجاء على خلاف منطوقهم،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r1.claim: Mecca's people were tested with famine through the Prophet's supplication against them; the garden owners were pious worshippers near San'a.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r1.anchor: إنا بلونا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع بدعوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r2.claim: Their father kept a year's food and gave the surplus to the poor, including missed grain, grapes, and dates; his sons feared hardship for their dependents and secretly swore to harvest early without leaving any share.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r2.anchor: فكان يأخذ منها قوت سنته ويتصدق بالباقي ، وكان يترك للمساكين ما أخطأه المنجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r3.claim: The sons did not make an exception in their oath, and God burned their garden; another report identifies them as Israelites.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r3.anchor: فحلفوا ليصرمنها مصبحين في السدف خفية عن المساكين ، ولم يستثنوا في يمينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r4.claim: They planned to harvest early in the dark before dawn; not making an exception means not saying ‘if God wills.’ Though a condition, it functions as an exception because the meanings coincide.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r4.anchor: { مصبحين } داخلين في الصبح مبكرين { ولا يستثنون } ولا يقولون إن شاء الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r5.claim: The calamity that swept the garden was a trial or destruction; the reading طيف varies from طائف.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r5.anchor: { فطاف عليها } بلاء أو هلاك { طئف } كقوله تعالى : { وأحيط بثمره }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r6.claim: الصريم may mean a garden cut down, a night-blackened garden, dried daytime vegetation, an empty garden, or sandy ground; صارمين means harvesters.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r6.anchor: { فأصبحت كالصريم } كالمصرومة لهلاك ثمرها . وقيل : الصريم الليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r7.claim: The phrase غدوا على حرثكم uses على because they went to cut and harvest it; alternatively غدا is understood as ‘turned toward,’ as in the expression ‘the enemy went against them.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن الغدو معنى الإقبال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r8.claim: يتخافتون means whispering; خفي, خفت, and خفد all denote concealment, and الخفدود is a bat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r8.anchor: { يتخافتون } يتسارون فيما بينهم . وخفى ، وخفت ، وخفد : ثلاثتها في معنى الكتم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r9.claim: The phrase أن لا يدخلنها is explanatory; Ibn Masud reads without أن, supplying ‘they say.’ The ban on a poor person entering means not allowing him in.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود بطرحها بإضمار القول ، أي تخافتون يقولون لا يدخلنها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r10.claim: حرد can mean a year withholding its good, camels withholding milk, or resolve and speed; the sons went out aiming to deprive the poor but found only deprivation themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r10.anchor: الحرد : من حردت السنة إذا منعت خيرها ؛ وحاردت الإبل إذا منعت درها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r11.claim: Another reading على حرد means they could manage only anger at one another, as in the next phrase ‘blaming one another.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p594/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( على حرد ) ، أي لم يقدروا إلا على حنق وغضب بعضهم على بعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r1.claim: A poetic line uses حرد for setting out quickly; birds called حراد are swift, so the sons thought they could promptly harvest and deny the poor their share.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r1.anchor: أقبل سيل جاء من أمر الله … يحرد حرد الجنة المغلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r2.claim: حرد may instead be the proper name of the garden, or mean that they assumed their planned harvest and deprivation would succeed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r2.anchor: وقيل : { حرد } علم للجنة ، أي غدوا على تلك الجنة قادرين على صرامها عند أنفسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r3.claim: They first thought they had lost their way because the ruined garden looked unlike theirs; after recognizing it, they admitted they had been deprived through their own wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r3.anchor: { إنا لضالون } أي ضللنا جنتنا ، وما هي بها لما رأوا من هلاكها ؛ فلما تأملوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r4.claim: أوسطهم means their most just and best member, from language for someone in the middle of their people; compare the description of the community as a middle community.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r4.anchor: { أوسطهم } أعدلهم وخيرهم ، من قولهم : هو من سطة قومه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r5.claim: لولا تسبحون most likely means remember God and repent of the corrupt plan; the speaker had urged them to repent before punishment, but they obeyed too late.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r5.anchor: لولا تذكرون الله وتتوبون إليه من خبث نيتكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes ‘glorify’ to mean making the exception ‘if God wills,’ since both entrusting matters to God and declaring His transcendence magnify Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r6.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالتسبيح . الاستثناء لالتقائهما في معنى التعظيم لله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says it means prayer; their neglect of prayer would explain why it did not restrain wrongdoing and prompt an exception.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن : هو الصلاة ، كأنهم كانوا يتوانون في الصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r8.claim: By saying ‘Glory be to our Lord,’ they deny that God is unjust and confess their own wrongdoing in withholding charity and failing to make an exception.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r8.anchor: { سبحان ربنا } سبحوا الله ونزهوه عن الظلم وعن كل قبيح ، ثم اعترفوا بظلمهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r9.claim: They blamed one another because some proposed the plan, some accepted it, some opposed it, and others remained silent in approval.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r9.anchor: { يتلاومون } يلوم بعضهم بعضا ؛ لأن منهم من زين ، ومنهم من قبل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r10.claim: The verb يبدلنا has readings with and without doubling; راغبون إلى ربنا means seeking good from Him and hoping for His pardon.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r10.anchor: { أن يبدلنا } قرىء بالتشديد والتخفيف { إلى ربنا راغبون } طالبون منه الخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r11.claim: Their punishment resembles that of Mecca's people and the garden owners, but the punishment of the afterlife is greater.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r11.anchor: { كذلك العذاب } مثل ذلك العذاب الذي بلونا به أهل مكة وأصحاب الجنة عذاب الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r12.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r12.claim: When asked whether the garden owners belong to Paradise or Hell, Qatada replied that the question had burdened him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r12.anchor: وسئل قتادة عن أصحاب الجنة : أهم من أهل الجنة أم من أهل النار ؟ فقال : لقد كلفتني تعبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r13.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r13.claim: Mujahid says the owners repented and were given a better garden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r13.anchor: وعن مجاهد : تابوا فأبدلوا خيرا منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r14.claim: Ibn Masud reports that they became sincere and God replaced the garden with one called al-Hayawan, whose grape clusters required a donkey to carry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p595/r14.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : بلغني أنهم أخلصوا وعرف الله منهم الصدق فأبدلهم بها جنة يقال لها الحيوان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r1.claim: The people tested may be Meccans whom God twice tested with famine, as the garden owners were tested until their garden became ashes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r1.anchor: أحدهما : إن الذين بلوناهم أهل مكة بلوناهم بالجوع كرتين , كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة حتى عادت رمادا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r2.claim: The people tested may instead be Quraysh at Badr; Ibn Jurayj relates that Abu Jahl urged capture and binding without killing, and God made the garden owners their example.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنهم قريش ببدر . حكى ابن جريج أن أبا جهل قال يوم بدر خذوهم أخذا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r3.claim: The garden was in Darwan, a Yemeni village twelve miles from Sana'a.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r3.anchor: هذه الجنة حديقة كانت باليمن بقرية يقال لها ضروان , بينها وبين صنعاء اليمن اثنا عشر ميلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r4.claim: One account says the garden belonged to a group of Abyssinians.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r4.anchor: وفيها قولان : أحدهما : أنها كانت لقوم من الحبشة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r5.claim: The garden belonged to an Israelite elder who kept enough for his family and gave the surplus away; his sons criticized him, inherited the garden, and vowed to harvest before the poor could come.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r5.anchor: الثاني : قاله قتادة أنها كانت لشيخ من بني إسرائيل له بنون , فكان يمسك منها قدر كفايته

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r6.claim: The heirs vowed to cut the garden's fruit in the morning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r6.anchor: أي حلفوا أن يقطعوا ثمرها حين يصبحون

MUQATIL:68:17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17/r1.claim: God tested the people of Mecca with famine as He tested the garden owners; their orchard perished.
MUQATIL:68:17/r1.anchor: ثم رجع في التقديم، فقال: { إنا بلوناهم } يقول: إنا ابتليناهم يعنى أهل ممكة بالجوع { كما بلونا }

MUQATIL:68:17/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17/r2.claim: The garden, called al-Sarim, had palms, crops, and grapes, lay two leagues from Sana in Yemen, and was inherited from their fathers.
MUQATIL:68:17/r2.anchor: كان فيها نخل وزرع وأعناب، ورثوها عن آبائهم، واسم الجنة الصريم،

MUQATIL:68:17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17/r3.claim: The owners were Muslims after Jesus; their forebears were righteous and gave poor people the gleanings missed by pickers, sickles, wind, and harvesters.
MUQATIL:68:17/r3.anchor: وكانوا مسلمين، وهذا بعد عيسى ابن مريم، عليه السلام، كان آباؤهم صالحين، يجعلون للمساكين من الثمار والزرع

MUQATIL:68:17/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17/r4.claim: Because they thought their dependents were many and the food plentiful, the owners planned to harvest secretly and not alert the poor who gathered for harvest.
MUQATIL:68:17/r4.anchor: فقال القوم: كثرت العيال، وهذا طعام كثير، أغدوا سرا جنتكم فاصرموها، ولا تؤذنوا المساكين،

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r1.claim: They swore to cut down the garden early the next morning.
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r1.anchor: { إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين } [آية: 17] ليصرمنها إذا أصبحوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r1.claim: God tested Mecca's people with famine and hunger after the Prophet prayed that Mudar suffer hardship like Joseph's years.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r1.anchor: امتحنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع حتى أكلوا الجيف والرمم بدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r2.claim: The garden belonged to people of Ṣarwān near Ḍarwān outside Ṣanʿāʾ; their father took his family's food and gave the rest to the poor.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r2.anchor: هم قوم من أهل الصلات كانت لأبيهم هذه الجنة بقربة يقال لها ضرو أن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r3.claim: After their father died, the sons feared poverty and resolved to harvest secretly at dawn before the poor appeared; they did not make an exception.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r3.anchor: فلما مات قال بنوه أن فعلنا ما كان يفعل أبونا ضاق علينا الامر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the owners were unbelievers, while the majority holds they were otherwise; the blight destroyed their orchard.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#5/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن كانوا كفارا والجمهور على الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r1.claim: The parable addresses Meccans: wealth was a test meant to elicit gratitude, but their arrogance and hostility to Muhammad were followed by famine and drought.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r2.claim: The garden story was locally known: a Yemenite owner gave God’s due, but after his death his sons withheld it and God destroyed the orchard.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r2.anchor: وكانت لرجل يؤدي حق الله تعالى منها فلما مات صارت إلى ولده، فمنعوا الناس خيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r3.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi locates the garden two farsakhs from Sanaa and says God burned it.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r3.anchor: كان بينهم وبين صنعاء فرسخان ابتلاهم الله بأن أحرق جنتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r4.claim: Another account places the garden at Dawran, one farsakh from Sanaa, and says its owners were miserly after Jesus was raised.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r5.claim: One account says the owners harvested at night to keep the poor away; at dawn they found the garden uprooted and blackened.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r5.anchor: وكانوا بخلاء فكانوا يجدون التمر ليلا من أجل المساكين

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r7.claim: One account says Gabriel swept the garden away, circled it around the Kaaba, and placed it where Taif now stands, explaining its name and fertility.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r7.anchor: وكان الطائف الذي طاف عليها جبريل عليه السلام فاقتلعها

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r8.speaker: البكري
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r8.claim: Al-Bakri instead derives Taif’s name from a man of Sadaf who built a wall around the town.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r8.anchor: سميت الطائف لأن رجلا من الصدف يقال له الدمون، بنى حائطا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r9.claim: Qurtubi says harvesters should share crops with poor people present, based on 6:141; the right is distinct from zakat, and he prefers the view that night harvesting was prohibited to avoid depriving them.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r9.anchor: وإنما قلنا الأول أصح لأن العقوبة كانت بسبب ما أرادوه من منع المساكين

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r4.claim: They meant to cut the date clusters at dawn under night’s dimness; sarm means cutting, and asrama means that the palms are ready to harvest.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r4.anchor: ليقطعن ثمر نخيلهم إذا أصبحوا بسدفة من الليل لئلا ينتبه المساكين لهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p207/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p207/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p207/r1.claim: The garden was an orchard in Yemen. Its former owner kept his annual food and gave the surplus to the poor; reports also describe generous gleanings left for them, which accumulated substantially.
ZAJJAJ:v5p207/r1.anchor: والجنة: البستان، وهؤلاء قوم بناحية اليمن

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r10.claim: The garden story also exemplifies God’s trial of Mecca: after the Prophet prayed against Muḍar for years of hardship like Joseph’s, God afflicted them with disease, death, and lost provisions.
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r10.anchor: فقال: اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر واجعلها عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r1.claim: God gave the wealthy man money and children as a test, intending gratitude and obedience; those who fail are stripped of blessings and afflicted.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r1.anchor: إنما أعطاه المال والبنين على سبيل الابتلاء والامتحان

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r2.claim: The orchard owners were tested to thank God and give the poor their due, just as the wealthy man should have used his blessings rightly.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r2.anchor: كما كلفنا أصحاب الجنة ذات الثمار ، أن يشكروا

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r3.claim: One report says a Muslim man of Thaqīf owned a fertile estate near Ṣanʿāʾ and regularly gave the poor a generous share at harvest; after his death, his sons withheld it and God burned the orchard.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r3.anchor: روي أن واحدا من ثقيف وكان مسلما

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r4.claim: Another report says the orchard owners were Israelites.

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r5.claim: Muqātil says they planned to go secretly at dawn, cut the harvest, and keep the poor from learning of it; ṣaram means cutting fruit, and aṣrama means the palms are ready to harvest.

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.claim: Most commentators say they did not make an exception by saying 'if God wills' because they were overconfident they could harvest; another view says they refused to set aside the poor's usual share.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.anchor: فالأكثرون أنهم إنما لم يستثنوا بمشيئة الله تعالى

ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n11/r1.claim: God tests the garden owners by giving them affluence far beyond their moral deserts.
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n11/r1.anchor: by bestowing on them affluence out of all proportion to their moral deserts

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.claim: God tested the Quraysh disbelievers as He tested the garden owners: they swore to harvest at dawn and did not say “if God wills.”

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the owners were Ethiopians whose father fed the poor from his garden; after he died, his sons called him foolish and vowed to exclude the poor.
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.anchor: هم ناس من الحبشة كانت لأبيهم جنة كان يطعم المساكين منها

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.claim: Qatāda says the garden belonged to a charitable old man; his sons opposed his charity and, after his death, set out to keep poor people away.
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.anchor: كانت الجنة لشيخ، وكان يتصدق، فكان بنوه ينهونه عن الصدقة

TAB-FULL:v23p173/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the garden owners were People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r1.anchor: كانوا من أهل الكتاب والصرم: القطع

TAB-FULL:v23p173/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r2.claim: The root ṣ-r-m means cutting; here they intended to gather or pick the garden's fruit.

TAB-FULL:v23p173/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r3.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses ṣaram for cutting off or severing a relationship, illustrating the root's meaning.
TAB-FULL:v23p173/r3.anchor: والصرم: القطع، وإنما عنى بقوله: {ليصرمنها} [القلم: 17] ليجدن ثمرتها

TABATABAI:68:17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r1.claim: The surah consoles the Prophet after the polytheists accuse him of madness, promises reward and honors his great character, forbids compliance and compromise with them, and commands patience for God's judgment.
TABATABAI:68:17/r1.anchor: تعزي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إثر ما رماه المشركون بالجنون

TABATABAI:68:17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r2.claim: The surah's overall context is Meccan; the author considers it plausible that the seventeen verses about the garden owners were revealed in Medina.
TABATABAI:68:17/r2.anchor: ولا يخلو من وجه بالنسبة إلى الآيات السبع عشرة

TABATABAI:68:17-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r3.claim: The garden episode is a warning to the Prophet's deniers: like its owners, they arrogantly rely on wealth, children, and apparent causes without gratitude, then face sudden punishment, useless possessions, regret, and repentance too late.
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r3.anchor: وعيد لمكذبي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الرامين له بالجنون

TABATABAI:68:17-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r4.claim: If these verses were revealed with the preceding passage, their warning applies to the deniers generally and recalls the surprise defeat at Badr as worldly proof that apparent causes fail.
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r4.anchor: حتى يأتيهم الأجل ويفاجئهم عذاب الآخرة أو عذاب دنيوي من عنده كما فاجأهم يوم بدر

TABATABAI:68:17-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r5.claim: Reports say the passage was revealed during a famine that struck Mecca after the Prophet prayed for years of hardship like Joseph's; the garden owners then parallel Mecca, though the final mutual blame does not fit easily.
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r5.anchor: وأما على ما رووا أن الآيات نزلت في القحط والسنة الذي أصاب أهل مكة وقريشا

TABATABAI:68:17-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r6.claim: Balāʾ can mean a test or the affliction itself; sarm is cutting fruit, istithnaʾ is excluding some from a general rule or saying if God wills, and a night visitor is a punishment arriving at night.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says Meccans were tested by famine just as the garden owners were; their garden was al-Ridwan in Yemen, nine miles from Sanaʿa.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عباس فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو هذا أنور في كتاب الله

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.anchor: فقال ابن عباس فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو هذا أنور في كتاب الله من الشمس الضاحية

THALABI:v10p16/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r1.claim: God tested the people of Mecca with famine and hunger, just as He tested the owners of the garden.
THALABI:v10p16/r1.anchor: إنا بلوناهم يعني اختبرنا وامتحنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r1.claim: The exegetes say God tested the people of Mecca with famine as He tested the orchard owners: a group of Thaqif in Yemen who inherited farmland and gardens from their Muslim father, who gave the poor a share at harvest and processing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r1.anchor: كما بلونا} (¬1) الآية. قال المفسرون: بلونا أهل مكة بالجوع والقحط كما ابتلينا أصحاب الجنة بالجوع حين هلكت جنانهم. وهم قوم من ثقيف، كانوا باليمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r2.claim: The heirs complained that their dependents were many and the wealth too little to keep giving to the poor as their father had, resolved to deprive them, and ended in ruin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r2.anchor: فقالت بنوه: العيال كثير، والمال قليل، ولا يسعنا أن نعطي المساكين كما كان يفعل أبونا. وعزموا على حرمان المساكين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r3.claim: Muqatil says the story is a parable for Meccan unbelievers to reflect on and return to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: وهذا مثل ضربه الله لكفار مكة ليعتبروا فيرجعوا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r4.claim: The exegetes name the orchard al-Darawan, near Sanaa; Saʿid ibn Jubayr puts it twelve miles away, while al-Kalbi says it was two farsakhs away and destroyed by fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p95/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: وهي تسمى (¬6): الضروان # بقرب صنعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r1.claim: They swore to cut their fruit in the morning at a late-night or pre-dawn darkness called سدفة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r1.anchor: حلفوا ليقطعن ثمر نخلهم إذا أصبحوا بسدفة (¬4) من الليل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r2.claim: Muqatil says they planned to go secretly early and harvest without notifying the poor, whereas their father used to tell the poor so they would gather.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: قالوا: اغدوا سرا إلى جنتكم فاصرموها ولا تؤذنوا المساكين وكان آباؤهم يخبرون المساكين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r3.claim: صرم means cutting a date bunch away from the palm; أرم النخل is used when the dates are ready to be cut.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r3.anchor: ويقال: قد صرم العذق عن النخلة وأرم النخل إذا حان وقت صرامه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r1.claim: God tested Mecca's people with drought and famine as He tested orchard owners in Yemen by burning their garden. Their father used to feed the poor from it; after he died, his sons feared giving would leave them short, so they planned to harvest before the poor came.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r1.anchor: { إنا بلوناهم } امتحنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع { كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة } كما امتحنا أصحاب البستان بإحراقها

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r2.claim: God tested the deniers who trusted in wealth and sons, making those supposed blessings a trial because they used them to block good and show pride rather than give thanks.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r2.anchor: Muhakkak ki Biz onlara bir belâ verdik yani mal ve oğullarına güvenip de öyle diyenleri

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r3.claim: At the first proclamation, Meccans followed such immoral leaders in denying God's signs and tormenting the Prophet, so he prayed for Mudar to face severe hardship like Joseph's years; God then afflicted them with seven years of famine.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r3.anchor: “Allahım! Mudar’a darbeni şiddetlendir ve onlara Yûsuf’un seneleri gibi kıtlık ver”[^32]

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r4.claim: The orchard story shows that this divine law is not a chance event limited to the deniers of Muhammad's time but applies across generations.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r4.anchor: sade onlara münhasır bir tesadüften ibaret olmayıp evvel ve âhir tatbik edilmesi iktizâ eden bir kanun olduğunu

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r5.claim: Here al-janna means an earthly paradise, a beautiful orchard, or at a deeper level a homeland; the story was familiar to Arabs, and its owners were those who possessed and managed the orchard.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r5.anchor: burada “cennet”ten murad dünya cenneti, güzel bağ ve bostan demektir. Daha derin bakışla da vatan demektir

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r6.claim: Calling them the plural owners, unlike the single owner's garden in al-Kahf, points to common property and a social or national parable rather than an individually managed estate.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r6.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’te وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ [18/35] âyetinde olduğu gibi bir ferd misâliyle getirilmeyip أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ diye cemi‘sîgasıyla müşterek bir milk misâli olarak getirilmesi

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r7.claim: The well-known account places the orchard near San'a in Yemen, at Sawran: a righteous owner gave God's due from its produce, but after his death his children withheld its benefit from people and begrudged God's due, bringing the narrated outcome.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r7.anchor: Yemen’de San‘â’ya yakın, Savran denilen arzda sâlih bir adamın güzel bir bağı vardı

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r8.claim: Beginning the social parable with the owners' oath points to how communal enterprises begin with an agreement whose guarantee is the oath and whose consequences govern profit and loss.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r8.anchor: her ictimâ‘î bir işin bir akid ve mukavele ile başladığını ve bunun yegâne müeyyidesi de yemin olduğunu

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r9.claim: The opening oath echoes the earlier “frequent swearer” and warns that people who make firm vows without considering their knowledge or power may swear falsely and bring disaster on themselves.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r9.anchor: yukarıda كُلَّ حَلَّافٍۢ en başında zikredilmiş olduğu gibi burada da ondan başlanmış

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r10.claim: Sarm means to cut or harvest a vine and its fruit, or sever something completely; although they meant to gather the fruit, their oath said they would certainly cut the garden itself in the morning.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r10.anchor: “Sarm” bağ kesmek, üzüm ve meyve devşirmek mânasına geldiği gibi, bir şeyi kökünden kesip tamamen ayırmak mânasına da gelir

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.claim: Their sworn plan came true, but to their harm and in an unforeseen way, not as they intended or by their own hand.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.anchor: Demek ki yemin ettikleri fiil olmuştu, fakat gönüllerindeki gibi ve kendi elleriyle lehlerine değil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r1.claim: The garden parable warns Meccan polytheists who failed to thank God for blessings; a pious owner shared harvest with the poor, but his sons planned to exclude them and a night calamity destroyed the crop.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r1.anchor: Hasat zamanı geldiğinde fakirleri çağırır, bahçenin ürünlerinden onlara ikramda bulunurdu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r2.claim: A report says the garden owner's sons invoked their large family to justify cutting the poor's share and secretly harvesting early, after which a disaster ruined the produce.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r2.anchor: oğulları, aile fertlerinin çokluğunu ileri sürerek yoksulların payını kesmeye ve bahçenin ürününü sabahleyin erkenden gizlice toplamaya karar vermişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r3.claim: God promises more blessings to the grateful and punishment to the ungrateful; the Meccan opponents lost prosperity and trade after rejecting the Prophet and eventually fell before Muslims.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r3.anchor: verdiği nimete şükredenlere daha fazla nimet vereceğini, nankörlük edenleri de cezalandıracağını haber vermiştir

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p309#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p309#2/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p309#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the land of the garden’s owners was in Yemen and called Ḍarwān.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p309#2/r3.anchor: عن معمر قال أخبرني تميم بن عبد الرحمن أنه سمع ابن جبير يقول هي أرض باليمن يقال لها ضروان

BINTSHATI:v2p62/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r1.claim: Balāʾ means affliction or trial, while ibtilāʾ means examination.

BINTSHATI:v2p62/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r2.claim: Janna first meant a worldly garden and derives from concealment, as seen in embryo, jinn, insanity, night, and a protective shield; the term later became the Islamic name for Paradise.
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r2.anchor: وترجع دلالة المادة في الأصل اللغوي إلى معنى الخفاء، يبدو بوضوح في الجنين مختفياً في رحم أمه، والجنون خفاء العقل، والجن جنس خفي من المخلوقات،

BINTSHATI:v2p62/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r3.claim: The Qur’an usually uses janna for Paradise, but also uses it for earthly gardens: singular in nine verses, dual in five, and plural twelve times; context decides.
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r3.anchor: وهو الاستعمال الغالب للفظ جنة وجنات في القرآن الكريم - نحو مائة وعشرين مرة - على أنها جاءت بدلالتها الأولى على الجنة المعروفة في الدنيا،

BINTSHATI:v2p62/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r4.claim: Ṣarm means cutting, especially harvesting crops and picking fruit, then developed a figurative sense.
BINTSHATI:v2p62/r4.anchor: والصرم: القطع، ومنه حصد الزرع وجني الثمر، ثم أخذ دلالته المجازية على

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p223/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p223/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p223/r3.claim: The garden owners’ oath in Sūrat al-Qalam is presented as sincere.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p223/r3.anchor: وكان أصحاب الجنة، في سورة القلم، صادقين:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r2.claim: She notes that ibtilāʾ also occurs in descriptions of the Last Day, and that fitna may come from God, Satan, magic, hypocrites, disbelievers, or people testing one another.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r2.anchor: وأما الفتنة فتكون من الله تعالى في مثل آيتى العنكبوت

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r3.speaker: الراغب وابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib and Ibn al-Athīr say balāʾ and fitna are used more often and more clearly for hardship; the author says her survey supports this, though testing through prosperity also occurs and can be paired with adversity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r3.anchor: وقول الراغب وابن الأثير، إن البلاء والفتنة أظهر في الشدة وأكثر استعمالا، يؤيده الاستقراء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r4.speaker: النبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r4.claim: A prophetic report says people endured a test through adversity and will also be tested through prosperity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p482/r4.anchor: ومنه الحديث: "ابتليتم بفتنة الضراء فصبرتم، وستبتلون بفتنة السراء"

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: The Hafs transmission of Asim is common across the eastern Islamic lands and many other countries, while Abu Amr's reading is used in Sudan near Egypt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: البلاد المصرية والهند وباكستان وتركيا والأفغان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: The Quran's description of its stories as the best indicates that they serve a higher purpose than entertainment, refreshment, or astonishment at events.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: أن القصص القرآنية لم تسق مساق الإحماض وتجديد النشاط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: A qissa is news of an event absent from the one reporting it, so accounts of events contemporaneous with revelation, such as Muslim battles, are not technically Quranic stories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: الخبر عن حادثة غائبة عن المخبر بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r4.claim: The plural of qissa is qiṣas with kasra on the first qaf; qaṣaṣ with fatḥa names the narrated report and is a verbal noun used for its object.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r5.claim: Quranic stories offer many lessons and communal benefits, select each story's noblest material, and omit the rest to avoid telling stories for amusement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r5.anchor: إن في تلك القصص لعبرا جمة وفوائد للأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r6.claim: Stories are dispersed among surahs and placed in contexts suited to their benefits, making them reminders and admonitions closer to preaching than to a chronological history book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r6.anchor: بل كانت مفرقة موزعة على مقامات تناسبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r7.claim: Narratives placed in their fitting contexts gain the force of proof and explanation while serving the Quran's original purposes, including legislation and its applications.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r7.anchor: سوقها في مناسباتها يكسبها صفتين : صفة البرهان وصفة التبيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r10.claim: The first benefit is that Quranic knowledge of prophets and earlier peoples challenged the People of the Book, broke their objections, and ended their portrayal of Muslims as an unlearned nation; earlier exegetes had not noted this benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p63/r10.anchor: فكان اشتمال القرآن على تلك القصص التي لا يعلمها إلا الراسخون في العلم من أهل الكتاب تحديا عظيما لأهل الكتاب

ITQAN:v1p53/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p53/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v1p53/r1.claim: Al-Sha'bi is cited saying the verse is not about Abdullah ibn Salam and is Meccan.
ITQAN:v1p53/r1.anchor: وأخرج عن الشعبي قال ليس بعبد الله بن سلام وهذه الآية مكية

ITQAN:v1p53/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p53/r16.speaker: السخاوي
ITQAN:v1p53/r16.claim: Al-Sakhawi's Jamal al-Qurra lists the passage from “We tested them” through “they know” as Medinan in al-Qalam.
ITQAN:v1p53/r16.anchor: ن استثني منها ﴿ إنا بلوناهم ﴾ إلى ﴿ يعلمون ﴾ ومن ﴿ فاصبر ﴾ إلى ﴿ الصالحين ﴾ فإنه مدني حكاه السخاوي في جمال القراء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r1.claim: Jurjani attributes the flaws in lines criticized for bad composition, including examples attributed to al-Mutanabbi and Abu Tammam, to violating the rules governing order, omission, and related choices.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r1.anchor: وفي نظائر ذلك مما وصفوه بفساد النظم ، وعابوه من جهة سوء التأليف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r2.claim: Correctness and excellence in composition likewise come from following those rules; نظم consists in observing the relations and meanings that govern words together.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p78/r2.anchor: ثبت أن ليس هو شيئا غير توخي معاني هذا العلم وأحكامه فيما بين الكلم

DAMGHANI:v1p110/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r6.claim: Al-janna can mean an earthly garden or orchard; the owners in this verse are owners of an orchard.
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r6.anchor: الثاني الجنة البستان في الدنيا قوله تعالى في سورة ق إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة يعني أصحاب البستان

DAMGHANI:v1p271/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r6.claim: Muṣbiḥīn means at dawn, after the night has passed; the parallel garden passage says it had become so by morning.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r6.anchor: فوجه منها من الغدو بعدما ذهب عنهم الليل قوله تعالى في سورة ق اذ اقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين يعني بالغداة

DAMGHANI:v1p271/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r15.claim: The aṣḥāb entry also lists companion, Prophet, brother, wife, storekeeper, and parents as senses, without expanding them in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r15.anchor: صحب على ثمانية اوجه السكان القوم الرفيق النبي صلة الله عليه وسلم الاخ الزوجة الخزان الابوان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r1.claim: The basic sense of أصبح is to reach the morning; it can also mean to kindle a lamp.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r1.anchor: الأصل في أصبح : إدراك الصباح للمصبح ، ويقال : أصبح ، إذا أوقد المصباح

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Jahl ordered captives tied up rather than killed at Badr; the garden parable was revealed about their power over the captives, like the garden owners’ power over their garden.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج ان أبا جهل قال يوم بدر خذوهم أخذا فاربطوهم في الحبال ولا تقتلوا
